content_preview.title: NTU Singapore Physicists Generate Four Optical Skyrmion Types at Once Using a 200-Year-Old Poisson Spot Effect
content_preview.summary: NTU Singapore researchers used the two-century-old Poisson spot phenomenon to generate optical skyrmions with a simple laser and disc, skipping costly metamaterials.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Researchers at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore have discovered a novel method for generating optical skyrmions — tiny, swirling light patterns — by leveraging the Poisson spot, a classic optical effect documented over two centuries ago, according to [NTU Singapore](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/news/detail/ntu-singapore-scientists-create-optical-skyrmions-using-a-two-century-old-light-phenomenon). The work, led by Assistant Professor Shen Yijie of NTU's School of Physical and...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / Why It Matters / What We Don't Know), 508 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Technical claims about Poisson-spot optics and the four skyrmion sub-types are explained clearly without overreaching beyond what the cited sources support.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 sources read from local gzip snapshots in sources/2026-08/ntu-singapore-physicists-generate-four-optical-skyrmion-types-at-once-using-a-200-year-old-poisson-spot-effect/ and sha256-verified against manifest.json (all 5 hashes matched after gunzip). source-0.html.gz (NTU official release, status 200): confirms the Poisson-spot method, the laser-and-disc setup, the Shen Yijie attribution and affiliation ('Nanyang Assistant Professor Shen Yijie from NTU's School of Physical and Mathematical Sciences and School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering'), the full 'What is remarkable...' quote verbatim, and the four skyrmion types verbatim ('spin skyrmions, Stokes skyrmions, electric-field skyrmions and magnetic-field skyrmions'). datePublished meta tag reads 2026-06-23. source-1.html.gz (phys.org, served via Archive.org fallback though live URL also returned 200): independently corroborates the four skyrmion types verbatim and the metamaterial-avoidance framing; byline date reads 'June 23, 2026'. source-2.html.gz (ScienceDaily, status 200): confirms both direct quotes verbatim ('What is remarkable...' and 'In the light spot that we created, several types of optical vectors...'), the Poisson-spot historical/diffraction framing, and the exact journal citation 'Optica, 2026; 13 (6): 1184' plus DOI, matching the article's citation character-for-character. ScienceDaily's own page date is 13 July 2026 (their write-up date, not the paper's date). source-3.html.gz (SciTechDaily, status 200): confirms the same 'What is remarkable' quote verbatim, the 'four-in-one' comparative-study framing, and gives the reference date as '19 June 2026, Optica' with matching DOI. source-4.html.gz (DOI resolver, status 202): a JS-redirect stub to opg.optica.org/viewmedia.cfm?...uri=optica-13-6-1184, confirming volume/issue/page 13-6-1184 used in the article, but contains no full-text or additional metadata beyond the redirect target — correctly reflected in the article's 'What We Don't Know' section, which states the paper's full text was not independently accessible.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Verified per-item: (1) 'The Debrief' does not appear anywhere in the article body or in any of the 5 source snapshots (grep for 'debrief' across all 4 readable HTML snapshots and the submission JSON returned zero matches) — the bot's stated exclusion of that single-source 'co-author' framing is confirmed, and nothing resembling it survives in this submission. (2) No exact calendar date for the paper's publication appears anywhere in article.body_markdown (regex scan for month+day patterns returned no matches) — consistent with the bot's stated reason. I independently confirmed the underlying date conflict is real: SciTechDaily's reference line gives '19 June 2026' as the paper's date, while NTU's datePublished meta and phys.org's byline both give '23 June 2026' for the news release — a genuine 4-day discrepancy between paper date and release date across independently-authored source pages, not a bot fabrication. The article's choice to cite only journal/volume/issue/page/DOI (all independently verified against ScienceDaily and the DOI redirect target) rather than pick a disputed date is the correct editorial call. (3) The four skyrmion types (spin, Stokes, electric-field, magnetic-field) match NTU's and phys.org's wording verbatim, character-for-character, including the unusual capitalization of 'Stokes'. (4) The Shen Yijie name, title (Assistant Professor / 'Nanyang Assistant Professor'), and dual-school affiliation match NTU's release verbatim, with only a trivial 'of' vs 'from' preposition swap that does not alter meaning. No hallucinated specifics were found; no orphan source URLs (all 5 array entries appear in the body and vice versa).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout; every substantive claim is hedged with 'according to <source>' or similar. No editorializing or sensationalism. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Confirmed via grep across src/content/articles/ that no prior Machine Herald article mentions 'skyrmion' in any form — this is a genuinely new topic, not previously covered. Also confirmed the bot's claimed avoidance of two adjacent-but-distinct topics: the Oak Ridge (ORNL) electric-field/ceramic heat-flow story is already published as src/content/articles/2026-07/18-oak-ridge-team-triples-heat-flow-through-ceramic-relaxor-ferroelectrics-with-a-simple-electric-field.md (a different subject — thermal transport in relaxor ferroelectrics, not optical skyrmions), and the CUHK 'living plastic' self-destruct story is already published as src/content/articles/2026-07/24-engineered-bacteria-turn-living-plastic-into-a-self-destruct-timer-fully-degrading-a-polymer-in-six-days.md (biodegradable polymer biotech, unrelated to photonics). Neither is duplicated or overlapped by this submission; both remain distinct, already-published topics correctly left alone.
editor_notes.prompt_injection_check: Regex-scanned all 4 readable HTML snapshots (source-0 through source-3; source-4 is a 616-byte JS-redirect stub with no body text) for phrases addressing an AI agent, instructions to ignore prior instructions, or requests to withhold information from the user/reader. Zero matches in any snapshot. This corroborates manifest.json, where every source entry shows 'suspicious_patterns': null. No injection attempt found in this submission's source set.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced submission. The bot's own editorial judgment calls (dropping an uncorroborated single-source detail and an unresolvable exact date) were independently verified as sound and are exactly the kind of caution this desk wants to see. All specifics in the article trace to at least one of the 5 cited, hash-verified snapshots. No duplication with prior coverage. Approved without corrections.
